findings.title: website_name leaks the website for TL0 users seen by anonymous viewers
findings.description:
`website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111). The generated `include_website?` returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true, which means a TL0 user seen by an anonymous viewer (`lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58-60`). The new `website_name` attribute is not in that list, and its condition only checks `website.present?`. For that same viewer, the host and path are still serialized, which is the information the gate exists to hide.

This reaches the page. For a TL0 user, `isBasic` is true, so `linkWebsite` is false and `user.hbs:71` prints `{{model.website_name}}` in a span. The JSON endpoint (`app/controllers/users_controller.rb:55`) and the HTML preload (`:51`) both use this serializer, so one fix covers both.

The spec does not catch this. The untrusted-attributes list (`spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11`) omits `website_name`. The fabricator never sets `website` (`spec/fabricators/user_profile_fabricator.rb:1-3`), so the existing test passes without exercising the gate even for `website`.

Fix: add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` call at line 105, delete the explicit `include_website_name` at line 153 (see the next finding), and add a TL0 case that sets `user.user_profile.website` and asserts `website_name` is absent.

findings.title: include_website_name is misnamed, so its presence check never runs
findings.description: Every other condition method in this file ends in `?` (for example lines 117, 161, 201, 223), and the macros at lines 9, 18, and 27 generate `include_<attr>?`. The serializer library calls `include_<name>?`. The method at line 153 is `def include_website_name` with no `?`, so it is never called. The `include_website_name?` hook keeps its default of true, so `website_name` is always emitted, as `null` when the website is blank. The spec does not test a blank website, so this goes unnoticed. This finding rests on the library's naming convention and the file's own pattern, not on a run.

findings.title: website_name logic repeats URI parsing and is hard to follow
findings.description:
The method parses `URI(website.to_s)` four times (lines 138, 143, 146, 149) and repeats `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` three times. The domain-matching rule is two inline ternaries with split/join chains, and it lives in the serializer. Two smaller issues in the same method:
- `"." << website_host` (line 149) mutates a string literal. `".#{website_host}"` expresses the same thing without mutation.
- The host comparison is case-sensitive, so `Example.com` and `example.com` do not match.

Suggested fix: parse the URI once into a local, and move the domain-matching rule into a small method (for example on `UserProfile`) so it can be unit-tested without the serializer.

findings.title: Specs miss the sibling-subdomain branch, the blank case, and the access gate
findings.description:
The three cases cover the exact-host, parent-domain, and host-only paths. The `elsif` at `user_serializer.rb:144-146` (same label count, both deeper than two labels) is never exercised, in either outcome. Missing cases:
- `blog.example.com` on `forum.example.com` should return `blog.example.com/user`.
- `blog.example.com` on `forum.other.org` should return `blog.example.com`.
- A blank website should produce no value. Currently it produces `null`.
- The TL0 anonymous context (lines 6-16) never sets a website, so it cannot catch a leak (see the first finding).

The context title "has a website name" (line 76) does not describe a behavior.

findings.title: Rescue modifier catches every StandardError
findings.description: `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` swallows any `StandardError` from the expression. The only expected failure is `URI::InvalidURIError`, so `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` would state the intent and avoid masking unrelated bugs.

findings.title: Frontend migration from websiteName is complete
findings.description: A repo-wide search finds no remaining `websiteName` references. The controller property is gone, the template uses `model.website_name` in all three places, and the model doc comment that wrongly said `@property websiteName` now says `profileBackground`. I did not run the Ember build or the qunit suite.
